Alex —

Thanks for the doc and the clear asks. Looping in Laura (Private Deployments) and Marissa (Partner Eng) to scope the validation work. First impressions after a quick skim:

- Network: the VPC peering section looks standard but we need the exact CIDR ranges and whether you plan NAT gateways for egress.
- Model profile: we generally recommend int4 quantized variants for 6B-8B models for this class of latency targets; include latency SLOs and token mix to validate.
- Acceptance tests: please include sample prompt sets for client-sensitive flows so we can run quality checks alongside throughput tests.

Could you attach your performance harness and a short checklist of what a clean run looks like? We prefer to run an initial smoke pass internally, then invite Polaris to a joint session.

Proposed next step: 30-min kickoff on Oct 13 to align owners and pick the first test window. Does 10:00 AM PST or 2:00 PM PST work for you?

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks Karthik — 10:00 AM PST on Oct 13 works for me. I attached the performance harness and a short test script (polaris-test-script.xlsx) that maps scenarios to pass/fail criteria. Quick answers to your questions:

- CIDR ranges: 10.40.0.0/16 for Polaris services; we will NAT through our egress subnet when calling external APIs.
- Token mix and SLOs: average request length 250 tokens, peak 600 tokens; latency target p95 <= 240ms for single-request flows.
- Ports: our harness needs outbound access to port 8500 and 443; no inbound ports required to Redwood Dedicated.

We can also provide a trimmed prompt set that excludes client PII for the quality checks.

Attachments: polaris-test-script.xlsx

Looking forward to the kickoff. If you want to share an agenda ahead of time, I can prep Polaris engineers.

Best,
Alex
Alex Navarro
Head of Integrations, Polaris Consulting

Alex — thanks for the prompt answers and attachments. Quick summary and proposed acceptance checklist so everyone is aligned before the Oct 13 kickoff:

Acceptance checklist (high level):
- Network connectivity: verify egress to ports 8500 and 443 from Polaris test harness; confirm CIDR and NAT behavior.
- Functional correctness: run trimmed prompt set (no PII) and validate coherent output against baseline quality metrics.
- Performance: execute the Polaris harness under three load profiles (baseline, sustained, spike) and meet p95 latency <= 240ms and token-cost within expected budget.
- Failover: validate fallback to smaller quantized model with acceptable degradation and no service disruption.

Owners and rough schedule:
- Redwood infra validation: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com) — smoke/pass/fail and network validation.
- Partner eng coordination and test orchestration: Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com).
- Polaris test run and artifacts: Alex Navarro (alex@polaris-consulting.com).

We will create a shared Drive folder and upload Redwood's runbook and ingestion whitelist by EOD Monday. Please confirm the kickoff time (10:00 AM PST on Oct 13) and we will send a calendar invite. Also linking the HubSpot deal for visibility: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8241
